Overcoming Google Ads Policy Limits in Healthcare Campaigns for Peak PPC Success

The healthcare industry is incredibly competitive, and now, with the rise of AI, even more changes are happening in how search engines rank and display information. Search engine policies are shifting, and organic SEO, while still important, can take time to bring your website to the first page of Google. That’s why many healthcare providers turn to Google Ads, or pay-per-click (PPC), to reach patients more quickly.

However, running PPC campaigns in the healthcare space comes with its own set of challenges. One of the most common obstacles is facing ad restrictions, often after the campaign has already been set up. These issues can be frustrating, especially when your ads are professionally written and your services are legitimate.

In the world of digital marketing, healthcare businesses like ALPHA Heart Center often face more scrutiny than other industries. Even when everything appears to follow the rules, you may still receive policy notices such as “Eligible (Limited)” or even full disapprovals. These restrictions can limit your campaign’s reach and performance.

That’s where expert guidance really makes a difference. At WevTEC, we not only fix website errors, but we also provide specialized healthcare SEO and PPC services for healthcare clinics and medical professionals. We understand the unique challenges that healthcare advertising presents, and we’ve spent years helping clinics overcome these obstacles successfully.

This blog was created to share that hands-on experience. Whether you are just starting out with Google Ads or are trying to troubleshoot limitations, the insights provided here will help you run compliant, high-performing campaigns that bring in real results.

This guide will explain why Google restricts healthcare ads, how to handle these issues strategically, and how to optimize your campaign for maximum PPC performance—while remaining 100% policy-compliant. Let’s break it down.

Why Are Healthcare Ads Restricted on Google?

Google Ads applies tight restrictions to healthcare content to:

  • Protect user safety and privacy

  • Comply with global health advertising laws

  • Prevent the spread of false or misleading medical claims

  • Restrict access to certain types of regulated products (like prescription medications)

Even if your campaign promotes general medical services—like cardiology consultations—Google’s algorithm might flag your ads due to:

  • Use of words like “treatment,” “prescription,” or “diagnosis”

  • The business name (e.g., “Heart,” “Medical,” “Clinic”)

  • Inclusion of a medical logo or symbol in ad creatives

  • Geotargeting in restricted countries

  • Lack of advertiser verification

Understanding Common Google Ads Healthcare Restrictions

Here’s what you might encounter:

Eligible (Limited)

Your ad is approved but can only run in specific countries or on certain devices. This is common for ads that mention medical terms or healthcare services, even if they’re compliant.

Disapproved

Your ad is completely blocked from running. This typically means there’s a clear policy violation—like promoting unapproved treatments or using restricted drug terms.

Under Review

Google’s system is evaluating the ad. You may need to wait up to 48 hours before knowing the final status.

Why ALPHA Heart Center Might Be Restricted

Even though ALPHA Heart Center is a legitimate, board-certified cardiology practice, your campaign might be flagged because:

  • Your business name contains the word “Heart,” which may be associated with medical procedures or treatments.

  • Your ad may use phrases like “treats high blood pressure” or “advanced cardiac care,” which Google’s systems automatically associate with restricted medical content.

  • The landing page or logo may resemble content that’s regulated (e.g., use of red crosses, stethoscope icons, etc.).

Step-by-Step: How to Handle Restrictions and Get Your Ads Approved

Understand Google’s Healthcare Policies

Start with the Google Healthcare and Medicines policy. Pay special attention to sections on:

  • Medical services

  • Prescription drug promotion

  • Restricted health claims

  • Advertiser verification requirements

Verify Your Identity as a Healthcare Advertiser

Ensure that Google has verified your business. This includes:

  • Verifying your business name via your Google Ads account

  • Matching your Google Business Profile with your ad campaign

  • Ensuring consistency between your domain, ad creatives, and legal business name

If ALPHA Heart Center is a licensed medical clinic, include this information on your landing page and in your appeal.

Adjust Your Ad Copy

Avoid claims that sound like you are guaranteeing results or offering specific treatments. Instead of:

❌ “Cure your heart disease today”
Use: “Schedule your consultation with a board-certified cardiologist”

❌ “Fast treatment for high blood pressure”
Use: “Specialized care for cardiovascular health in [City]”

Keep your tone informative, not promotional. Stick to facts and avoid terms like “instant,” “miracle,” or “prescription.”

Prepare a Professional Appeal (If Limited)

If your ad is flagged as “Eligible (Limited)”, submit a detailed appeal. Here’s a sample you can use:

Sample Appeal Message:

We are running a campaign for ALPHA Heart Center, a licensed and board-certified cardiology clinic. Our ad asset group is marked as “Eligible (Limited)” possibly due to the inclusion of our business name or logo. However, our content does not promote restricted drug terms or unapproved treatments. We respectfully request a manual review to confirm that our campaign complies with Google Ads healthcare policies.

Check Your Landing Page for Compliance

Your landing page must be clear, secure, and policy-friendly. Include:

  • Credentials of the physician or medical team

  • Clear location and contact details

  • Secure HTTPS domain

  • Disclaimers, if needed (e.g., “This information is not a substitute for medical advice”)

  • No exaggerated medical claims or drug references

Review Geotargeting Settings

Some countries strictly regulate health-related ads. If your ad is targeting countries like Canada, the UK, or parts of Europe, this may trigger automatic limitations. Try narrowing your targeting to U.S.-based states and cities.

Optimization Tips to Boost PPC Performance (While Staying Compliant)

Even with policy filters in place, there are smart ways to drive results:

Use Location-Based Headlines

“Trusted Cardiologist in [City]” is safer and performs better than “Heart Treatment Expert”

Leverage Call Extensions and Call-Only Ads

Let people call your clinic directly without needing to click through.

Run Responsive Search Ads

Mix and match safe headline variations. Google will automatically prioritize compliant and high-performing ones.

Split-Test Ad Groups

Create multiple versions with slightly different headlines, assets, and target settings to find which version passes review and performs best.

Monitor Campaign Regularly

Watch for any changes in status or new policy notifications. Resolve them quickly to avoid disruption in delivery.

Final Thoughts: Balancing Compliance and Performance in Healthcare Ads

Advertising for a cardiology practice like ALPHA Heart Center on Google Ads isn’t impossible—but it does require a smarter, more policy-conscious approach. By understanding Google’s healthcare policies, making strategic ad adjustments, and appealing the right way, you can keep your campaigns live and productive.

And remember, restrictions don’t always mean rejection. Often, it’s just a matter of refining your content, verifying your identity, and demonstrating that you’re running a trustworthy, patient-focused practice.
